claims.claim: **CP — a motor disorder that does not progress — has many possible causes, so every child is investigated** to identify the cause and rule out progressive conditions.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The diagnosis is clinical, typically before 12–24 months**, though it is possible from 3 months of corrected gestational age.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The cause is non-progressive but clinical features evolve — review regularly for complications.** **Early intervention** helps infants who have CP or are at high risk of it.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer (using corrected age) for:** hand fisting or head lag still present after 4 months · cannot sit without support after 9 months · leg stiffness at 6–12 months · hand preference before 12 months · still not walking at 18 months.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider referral for:** a Moro reflex that persists past 6 months · asymmetric or toe-walking that is consistent past 12 months · persisting primitive reflexes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Think of another diagnosis (metabolic, neurodegenerative) if there is:** skill loss or progressive symptoms · dysmorphism · clear deterioration with illness or fasting · muscle atrophy · sensory loss · a family history of another genetic condition.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **MRI brain at term equivalent if impairment is severe or progressive**; consider repeating **after 2 years** if the first was normal, inconclusive or not done. At 2 years, the MRI is normal in about 10–15% of children with clinical CP.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Genetics: microarray first line**; if normal, consider whole exome sequencing (ideally trio) with or without genetics referral — a genetic cause may underlie 25% or more.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Other tests with the relevant specialist** where infection, metabolic or genetic causes are suggested — eg blood gas, CK, ammonia, urine metabolic screen; **thrombophilia screen for hemiplegia, infarct on imaging or a family history**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A multidisciplinary team is essential** — physiotherapy, occupational therapy and speech pathology, with dietitians, orthotists, social work, psychology, education and nursing.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Spasticity:** focal/segmental — **injected botulinum toxin**; generalised — **oral baclofen first line**. Intrathecal baclofen or selective dorsal rhizotomy are for rare cases, by rehab services.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dystonia (weak evidence):** focal — botulinum toxin; generalised — **oral baclofen first line**, adding **oral/transdermal clonidine or oral gabapentin** if insufficient.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Every child with CP needs hip surveillance.** Start with a clinical assessment at **12 months**, with or without an AP hip X-ray (not needed in GMFCS I); concerns prompt orthopaedic referral.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Greater motor impairment means greater risk** of hip dislocation and scoliosis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Knee surveillance:** watch for knee flexion deformity in GMFCS I–III from 5 years to skeletal maturity — it can cost the child walking.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Saliva control:** anterior drooling causes skin breakdown and social difficulty; posterior drooling causes choking and aspiration. **Consider anticholinergics**; botulinum toxin to the salivary glands or surgery in some.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Growth and feeding:** monitor growth and micronutrients; **consider enteral tube feeding** for weight gain, deficiencies, a medication route and to reduce aspiration.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Respiratory:** increased risk of aspiration, restrictive lung disease, recurrent chest infection and sleep apnoea. **Immunise, including yearly influenza vaccine.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **How common:** hearing loss about 10% · vision loss 30–50% · intellectual disability up to 45% · epilepsy up to 50%. Arrange regular audiology and ophthalmology.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Formal cognitive assessment and educational support**, ideally in the year before school.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Low bone density:** increased pathological fracture risk. **Check vitamin D yearly**; optimise calcium, exercise and sunlight.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Urinary incontinence** may need medical management or clean intermittent catheterisation for neurogenic bladder; consider urology referral.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the local paediatric team** for an infant with risk factors or features of CP, or a child needing admission.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy' (Last updated November 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23
